sentences.text: Barinasuchus is an extinct genus of sebecid mesoeucrocodylian, a member of the family Sebecidae.

The animal was heterodont, possessing two distinct types of teeth. The teeth of the premaxilla and front maxilla were longer and more conical than the shorter, thinner teeth further back. The mandible was very robust compared to other sebecids and widest at the fourth mandibular tooth. This dentition made it a formidable predator.
Due to the destruction of the holotype, the postcranial skeleton and much of the skull of Barinasuchus are unknown.
The genus was described by Paolillo and Linares in 2007, with the type species being B. arveloi.

Road workers near Qedabra Socó, Venezuela, discovered a large sebecid skeleton in 1973 while building a road to El Toro. However, the type specimen was largely destroyed during excavation, leaving only a partial snout and mandible.
The type specimen comes from the Miocene-age Parángula Formation.
Barinasuchus primarily inhabited lacustrine environments and lived in the Pebas Mega-Wetland and adjacent regions during the Miocene.

Barinasuchus was among the last and largest sebecids, outlasting others like Dentaneosuchus, possibly due to isolation. Barinasuchus and other similarly sized sebecosuchians appear to have been apex predators.

A 2025 analysis by Bravo et al. recovered Barinasuchus as the sister taxon to a clade containing the Lumbrera form and Sebecus species. In a cladogram, Barinasuchus is classified as a Sebecosuchian of the family Sebecidae, closely related to the genus Lorosuchus and forming the sister taxon to the genera Ayllusuchus and Bretesuchus, indicating it represents a fairly basal lineage within the family.

Barinasuchus lived in Argentina, Peru, and Venezuela from the middle Eocene to the Late Miocene, approximately 42 to 11.6 million years ago. Later specimens of Barinasuchus lived up to the middle Miocene in a northern South American ecosystem dominated by non-mammalian predators.
It is debated whether the extinction of Barinasuchus resulted from the loss of the Pebas Mega-Wetland or the diversification of mammalian predators and phorusrhacid birds.
